title: Staying alive to carry something forward
literal_meaning: If you yourself survive, your father’s name lives on.
explanation: The short line makes survival the condition for carrying a family name forward. The collection’s gloss extends the thought towards being able to help the world by first getting oneself ahead. This is a reminder that continuing to live and act matters; it does not establish that another person’s welfare is unimportant.
meaning_odia: ନିଜେ ବଞ୍ଚି ରହିଲେ ହିଁ ବାପର ନାଁ ଆଗକୁ ନେଇହେବ—ଛୋଟ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଏହି କଥା କହେ। ସବୁକିଛି କରିବାର ଆଗରୁ ନିଜର ରହିବା ଓ କାମ କରିପାରିବା ଦରକାର। ଏହି ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଏହାକୁ ନିଜେ ଆଗେଇ ପରର ମଙ୍ଗଳ କରିବା ସହ ଯୋଡ଼େ। କଥାର ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ଅନୁସାରେ କେହି ନିଜ ସ୍ୱାର୍ଥକୁ ଆଗରେ ରଖିବା ପାଇଁ ବି ଧାଡ଼ିଟି କହିପାରେ; ଉତ୍ସର ଏହି ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ସବୁ ବ୍ୟବହାରର ସୀମା ନୁହେଁ।
usage_example: Someone carrying out a long family task is exhausted but unwilling to stop. A relative uses the line to urge a pause so the work can continue tomorrow. (Original imagined example.)
cultural_context: The father’s name is the source’s family image, not a claim that only sons sustain families. English “lives on” supplies the implied continuation rather than an additional historical assertion. No origin story is supplied.
odia_summary: ନିଜେ ବଞ୍ଚି ଓ ସମର୍ଥ ରହିଲେ ହିଁ ଆଗକୁ କିଛି କରିହେବ।
english_summary: Survival makes continuing the family’s work possible.
